_meta.purpose: Evaluation set for CyberGuard's risk-scoring engine (src/lib/risk_engine.ts / .agents/risk_engine_py.py). This is a rule-based weighted-scoring formula, not a trained classifier, so 'evaluation' here means face validity against real, well-documented incidents plus internal consistency (monotonicity) — not train/test accuracy in the ML sense.
_meta.expected_severity_derivation: Ground-truth labels reflect real-world/industry consensus severity for each incident (CISA KEV inclusion, actual blast radius, published advisories), not just the formula's own output — the point is to check the formula agrees with reality on cases where reality is well documented.

cases.label: Log4Shell
cases.rationale: CVSS 10.0, mass active exploitation within days of disclosure (CISA KEV), trivial RCE on internet-facing Log4j-using services. Universally treated as an emergency 'patch now' event.

cases.label: EternalBlue / WannaCry (MS17-010)
cases.rationale: Weaponized in WannaCry and NotPetya, wormable SMB RCE. Even though CVSS (8.1) alone wouldn't clear the CRITICAL bar, confirmed active exploitation + public Metasploit module pushes it there — the formula is expected to weight threat-intel context heavily, not just CVSS.

cases.label: Heartbleed
cases.rationale: OpenSSL memory-disclosure bug affecting ~17% of internet-facing TLS servers at disclosure; actively exploited to steal private keys and session data from critical infrastructure.

cases.label: Apache Struts RCE (Equifax breach)
cases.rationale: Unpatched instance directly led to the 2017 Equifax breach (147M records). Maximum CVSS, trivial mass-scanned exploit, internet-facing critical asset.

cases.label: Internal service, POC exploit published, no confirmed exploitation
cases.rationale: A synthetic boundary case (not a real CVE): moderate CVSS with a published proof-of-concept but no evidence of in-the-wild use on a medium-criticality internal system. Should land in HIGH (24h remediation SLA), not CRITICAL — there is real risk but no confirmed active threat.

cases.label: Air-gapped system, high CVSS, no exploit available
cases.rationale: Demonstrates the network-exposure modifier: identical CVSS/asset-criticality to an internet-facing CRITICAL case, but no exploit exists and the asset is air-gapped — real-world risk is much lower despite the scary CVSS number, so the engine should downgrade it substantially.

cases.label: Low-CVSS misconfiguration, low-criticality internal test system
cases.rationale: Baseline sanity check — nothing about this case should trigger urgency. Confirms the formula doesn't over-alarm on low-stakes findings, which matters for analyst trust (alert fatigue).

cases.label: PrintNightmare
cases.rationale: Windows Print Spooler RCE/LPE with public exploit code and confirmed in-the-wild use across enterprise networks shortly after disclosure; treated as an emergency patch by CISA.
